clue.text: Lift pig and howl playfully in mock combat

indicators.note: doing something playfully means messing about rather than keeping things in order, so the letters are tossed around

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, without the joining 'and'

explanation.surface: Someone hoists a pig while it squeals, all as part of a play fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is only joining the fodder words; the letters of LIFT, PIG and HOWL rearrange to PILLOW FIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Children bashing each other with bedroom cushions is a harmless, pretend battle, nobody really hurt.

clue.text: Some clip-art I allow – not all

indicators.note: only some of the letters are wanted, a run sitting inside the longer phrase

blocks.note: the run starts at the last letter of the first word and ends inside the last

explanation.surface: Someone permits only a selection of the clip-art images to be used.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen and spaces are ignored: cliPART I ALlow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incomplete covers only a portion of the whole, which is exactly what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Drifting, leaderless, anchorless right away in lake

indicators.note: without a leader means the front letter is dropped
sending something away removes it from the word
things that drift float off out of position, so the letters wander into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, then trimmed
R is the standard abbreviation for right, and this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A boat with no skipper and no anchor drifts about on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: ANCHORLESS loses its first letter A and the R for right, leaving NCHOLESS, which rearranges to LOCH NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: This famous Scottish body of water, home of the fabled monster, is a lake; loch is the Scots word.

clue.text: Seeds explorer's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means sent out over the airwaves, so the word is heard rather than read

blocks.note: Captain Lawrence Oates was a member of Scott's doomed Antarctic expedition

explanation.surface: An explorer scatters seed by hand, broadcasting it across a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' also means sowing seed by scattering, which fits the surface perfectly but here it signals a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The grains of this cereal crop are its seeds, eaten as porridge or fed to horses.

clue.text: Corrosive liquid police found on kitchen surface

indicators.note: in a down entry one part sitting on another means it comes beneath it, so the parts follow one another

blocks.note: Formica is a brand of laminate used for worktops
the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Police discover a caustic fluid spilled on a kitchen worktop.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'on' means placed below, so the police letters come after the worktop material.
explanation.definitionFit: This acid, found in ant stings, is a caustic chemical that burns skin and eats into materials.

clue.text: Home of St Catherine, they say: d'you know her?

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the spelling comes from what is heard

blocks.note: slurred together, the question runs into the Italian port's name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are acquainted with a saint from her home town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Catherine of Genoa was a fifteenth-century Italian mystic; said quickly, 'd'you know her' comes out as the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The saint was born and lived her life in this Ligurian port city, so it was her home.

clue.text: Did he make up Tolman, Kíli and Ents? Not half!

definitions.text: Did he make up Tolman, Kíli and Ents? Not half!

indicators.note: keeping no more than half of each word means only its first half survives

blocks.note: first half of a six-letter name
first half of a four-letter name
first half of a four-letter word

explanation.surface: Did a certain author invent these characters? Not half — of course he did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'absolutely', but also instructs taking half of each name. Tolman Cotton, the dwarf Kíli and the tree-like Ents all appear in his books.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the novelist who created these Middle-earth characters, so the question points straight at him.

clue.text: Mama had a thing about spiritual adviser

indicators.note: about can mean round and around, so the letters are turned into a fresh order

blocks.note: the letters of all four words

explanation.surface: Mother was rather fixated on her guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had a thing about' reads as an idiom for being obsessed, but 'about' alone does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian independence leader was revered as a moral and religious guide; Mahatma itself means great soul.

clue.text: Crushed, and imposed our way of working

indicators.note: something crushed is broken and squashed out of shape, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A defeated side complains that the victors squashed them and forced their methods on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' looks like a link but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase names someone's habitual method or procedure, literally a mode of operating.

clue.text: Fruit loop runs, dividing with America First

indicators.note: a thing that divides another sits inside it, splitting it in two
placing something first puts it at the very front of the line-up

blocks.note: A is a common abbreviation for America
a picot is a small decorative loop of thread on lace or ribbon
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cereal hoop or a political slogan about putting America first, all mixed in one breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit loop' suggests the breakfast cereal, but the fruit is the definition. The runs letter splits PICOT after its P, and America's letter goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: This small orange stone fruit, related to the peach, is a fruit by any measure.

clue.text: Real's once; now a Liga division owner, primarily?

definitions.text: Real's once; now a Liga division owner, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: Real's once; now a Liga division owner
blocks.note: opening letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A former Real Madrid star is imagined as now owning a club in Spain's league.
explanation.walkthrough: Real is Real Madrid, the Spanish football club; La Liga is Spain's top division. The first letters of the seven words spell the player's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Cristiano Ronaldo played for Real Madrid, so he is Real's once; the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Non-native regularly seen in Dáil Éireann

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is picked out

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters, accents ignored

explanation.surface: A foreigner is spotted in the Irish parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil Éireann is the lower house of Ireland's parliament; the accents are ignored when taking every second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign national living in a country is legally termed this; both words describe someone from elsewhere.

clue.text: One sheep is eaten by you, French dish that's spongy

indicators.note: whatever is eaten ends up inside the one doing the eating

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a male sheep
taken as written
tu is the informal French for you

explanation.surface: A French diner is described tucking into some mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' does double duty in the surface but here gives its own two letters inside the French pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian dessert is built from sponge fingers soaked in coffee, so it is a spongy pudding.

clue.text: Bad-tempered hives beekeeper finally leaves in tree

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it
when something leaves it is gone, so that letter is taken out

blocks.note: a prickly person is touchy and irritable
hives is an itchy skin rash
the closing letter, which is removed

explanation.surface: An irritable beekeeper walks away from the hives up in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hives' pulls toward beehives, but it is the skin complaint, which loses the R ending 'beekeeper'.
explanation.definitionFit: This thorny North American shrub, also called toothache tree, is a kind of small tree.

clue.text: A little malingerer, Everyman will watch online channel

indicators.note: a little of a word is just a small taste of it, its opening letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
the setter speaking says I'll, short for I will
to stream a programme is to watch it over the internet

explanation.surface: A slight shirker, the setter says, will spend the day watching a streaming service.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so 'Everyman will' is I'LL with the apostrophe dropped. 'Channel' looks like a TV channel but is a water course.
explanation.definitionFit: A millstream is the current of water carried along to drive a mill wheel, a kind of artificial watercourse.

clue.text: Remove ties from hunting hound repeatedly, not good

indicators.note: repeatedly means the removal happens more than once, wherever that letter turns up
not means without, so that letter must be taken out

blocks.note: a gundog is trained to retrieve game for shooters
G is the usual abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Someone unties a hunting dog over and over because it is misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: Both G's are removed from GUNDOG, the first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfasten a knot or loosen laces is to untie it, so to release bindings.

clue.text: Preventing giving tip-off, victory for Luxembourg

indicators.note: one thing given for another means it is swapped in as a replacement

blocks.note: to tip someone off is to warn them
V is the familiar abbreviation for victory
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg, and it is the letter swapped out

explanation.surface: A tip-off is passed on that stops something bad, earning Luxembourg a win.
explanation.walkthrough: In the warning word, V takes the place of the L.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to stop it happening, so the two participles match exactly.

clue.text: Matter concealed by magistrate

indicators.note: what is concealed by something is tucked away inside it

blocks.note: letters three to six

explanation.surface: A judge keeps the substance of a case secret.
explanation.walkthrough: maGISTrate.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance or main point of a discussion is its essence, the central topic it concerns.

clue.text: Loud Australian wearing dresses for expeditions

indicators.note: what is wearing clothes has them wrapped around it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
A is a common abbreviation for Australian
saris are wrapped dresses worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: A brash Australian wears colourful dresses for her travels.
explanation.walkthrough: The loud and Australian letters sit inside the dresses, after their first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Safaris are organised journeys, typically to see wildlife in Africa, so they are expeditions.

clue.text: A vile beach resort within reach

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it says sort the letters again into another order

blocks.note: the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A grotty seaside resort is only a short trip away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beach resort' reads as a holiday spot, but 'resort' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attainable lies close enough to be grasped, a goal that can be accomplished.

clue.text: Reserve Grant a little reading

blocks.note: to book a seat is to reserve it
to let is to allow or grant permission

explanation.surface: Someone named Grant is held back as a replacement and is a slow reader.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Grant' suggests a person, but it is the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin book or pamphlet offers only a short amount of text, hence a light read.

clue.text: Economy supply, 50 florins

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, it says the letters bend flexibly into a new shape

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A budget is set at fifty florins, the old British two-shilling coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the noun here: it is supple-ly, flexibly. A florin was a pre-decimal British coin worth two shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy service, like a budget airline, is basic and stripped of extras, used here adjectivally.

clue.text: Children, go out

blocks.note: first meaning: offspring, as in dying without heirs
second meaning: to emerge or flow forth

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a parent sending the kids outside; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal language offspring are a person's descendants, and as a verb the word means to come forth or emerge.

clue.text: Big city German's agreeable expression offering wine

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian metropolis
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German visitor to a big city says yes when offered a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agreeable expression' means a word of agreement, not a pleasant face.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a Spanish red produced in the region of that name in northern Spain.

clue.text: Perhaps pop star Dido cold at heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the two central letters
the two central letters

explanation.surface: The singer Dido is said to be an icy person underneath.
explanation.walkthrough: Dido is a real British pop singer, which makes the definition sit naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop star adored by fans is an example of someone worshipped, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Recalled a small gentleman with a hot spicy paste

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters run back the other way

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the title of a knight, a gentleman
taken as written
H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A short gentleman is remembered alongside a fiery condiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the letter that ends up in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a fiery North African chilli condiment, a ground mixture of peppers and spices.

clue.text: What dentist will have done – trained?

blocks.note: first meaning: bored into a tooth
second meaning: taught by repeated practice, as soldiers are

explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic description of a past action, the second a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist bores into teeth with a rotating tool, and recruits schooled through repetitive exercises are disciplined the same way.

clue.text: Moderate rage first – get it?

indicators.note: first fixes which piece leads, the one named just before it going in front

blocks.note: to seethe is to rage inwardly
light as in mild or moderate

explanation.surface: Advice to calm your temper before anything else — understood?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate' reads as a verb telling you to calm down, but it is the adjective for mild.
explanation.definitionFit: To finally understand something is an idiom for a sudden realisation, like grasping a joke.
